_comment: Scoped TypeScript mutation testing, the frontend twin of src-tauri/mutants.toml (see that file's header for the philosophy). Mutates ONLY high-value pure-logic modules with real branching and solid unit tests — not the whole app, most of which is React/Tauri glue that mutation testing can't meaningfully evaluate from jsdom. Run weekly + on demand via .github/workflows/mutation.yml (ts-mutants job); non-blocking signal source, not a gate. Local run: pnpm mutation:ts (or narrow it: pnpm mutation:ts -- --mutate src/lib/lintEngine/linter.ts). Widen scope by appending globs to `mutate` once the current scope's kill rate is healthy.
_scopeNotes: extensions/claim.ts (90.8%) and extensions/resolve.ts (83.4%; 94% on logic once the error-message StringLiteral survivors are set aside) are the extension-registry core (ADR-015). resolve.ts's residual survivors are deliberate: ~2 dozen mutate exact error-message text (pinning those is brittle — the tests assert the error CODE + refused ordering instead), 2 are equivalent mutants on `byId.get(id)` undefined-guards (every ready/sorted id came from `order`, so the else-branch is unreachable), and the rest are cycle-detection DFS internals already covered behaviorally by the 6 `cycles` tests. Do NOT chase the 85% overall bar by asserting exact error strings.
